design.status_of_evidence: Lee2019 participants and pairs as in C3 (independent of HS-Stroke, not of C3/C4); ShallowConvNet and early-stopped EEGNet have never been run on these data
design.models: EEGNet-8,2 exactly as C2/C3b; ShallowConvNet (Schirrmeister 2017) at 128 Hz: temporal conv 40 x 13, spatial conv 40 x 40 x 20, BN, square, avg pool 37 / 7, log, dropout 0.5, dense; both: Adam 1e-3, batch 64, 100 epochs, no tuning; grouped exact equivalents (tests/test_r7_deep_group.py)
design.early_stopping: by selection: the epoch with minimum validation cross-entropy on 60 held-out base trials (30 per class, identical in every arm of a task); the final-epoch read-out comes from the same run
design.pairs: C3 pairs; per task an outcome-blind 5 of 40 (rng [7601, participant, run]); arms A, B, C, E + one A/A per task
design.inference: 54 participants; t95 CI; Monte Carlo sign-flip (1e6, seed 7499); Holm over the 6-test family

hypotheses_declared_before_any_fit.question: is the deep-decoder exact-copy effect (C2/C3b, EEGNet, fixed 100-epoch schedule) an artefact of the schedule or of one architecture?
hypotheses_declared_before_any_fit.H1: for EEGNet and ShallowConvNet, at both read-outs (final epoch; minimum-validation-loss epoch), d > 0
hypotheses_declared_before_any_fit.H2_declared_direction: early stopping reduces the effect: d_es - d_final < 0 for each model (two-sided test)
hypotheses_declared_before_any_fit.descriptive: placebo per model and read-out, BA contrast, context accuracy, off-target change, early-stopping epoch distribution, ShallowConvNet minus EEGNet, C3a TS+LR on the same pairs (different base: 300 vs 240 rows)
hypotheses_declared_before_any_fit.no_SESOI: no equivalence region and no post-hoc relevance threshold
